explanation: On a curved surface the rule breaks. A triangle drawn on a globe from the North Pole to two points on the Equator can have three right angles, adding up to 270 degrees.

claims.text: The interior angles of a triangle on a flat plane add up to 180 degrees.
The angles of a flat triangle never add up to 90, 270 or 360 degrees.
On a sphere, a triangle joining the North Pole to two points on the Equator a quarter of the way round from each other has three right angles, totalling 270 degrees.
